comments.text: 6:00 (neutral wire) could have been a typo by the examiner. Also, that dependent claim is not something you will hanging your hat on, so don't make a major issue out of it.  Focus the arguments on what you will ultimately be wanting protection wise.  Examiners don't care much for making a mountain out of a molehill regarding throw-away clams (i.e., wherein the result is displayed; wherein the thing is grounded; printing the result; etc.).   Keeping a good working relationship with the examiner is the best advice anybody could give, yet it's seldom discussed.  One way to keep a good working relationship is NOT to make EVERYTHING an 911 issue.  Focus, focus, focus, and overlook the little things that don't much matter.  Examiners are under production pressures, and make mistakes in the OA's.  So what.  Is the art spot on or not.  Applicant is responsible for reading the entire reference and embodiments relied upon by the examiner, even if they are not references in the OA.   Focusing, and don't nit pick - can get you a better patent faster.  Just a thought.
